rows.verified: Temporary works require the same degree of care and attention as permanent works.
Temporary works include access scaffolds, props, shoring, excavation support, falsework, formwork, haul roads and working platforms.
Temporary structures must be designed, installed and maintained to withstand foreseeable loads.
Temporary structures should be used only for the purposes for which they were designed, installed and maintained.
Temporary works such as scaffolding, excavations, cofferdams and caissons require regular inspection by a competent person.
Temporary works need to be planned and managed.
Management should coordinate design, equipment selection, contractors, supervision, completion checks, authorisation to load and removal.
A standard solution still requires verification that site conditions and design assumptions are valid.
Temporary-works controls depend on design assumptions, loads, ground, sequence, equipment, interfaces, inspection and change control.
Temporary-works evidence is design-, project- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level structural-failure probability.
COMAH requires businesses to take all necessary measures to prevent major accidents involving dangerous substances.
COMAH also requires businesses to limit consequences to people and the environment when major accidents occur.
COMAH applicability depends on named dangerous substances, hazard categories and threshold quantities.
All operators in scope have a general duty to prevent and mitigate major accidents.
Upper-tier establishments must prepare a safety report.
A safety report must describe the establishment and its environment, including relevant geographical and environmental conditions.
A safety report must describe credible major-accident scenarios and the events or conditions that could trigger them.
Upper-tier safety reports must include prevention, mitigation and emergency-planning arrangements.
COMAH applicability and controls depend on substance classification, inventory, thresholds, processes, site context and tier status.
COMAH evidence is establishment-, inventory- and scenario-specific and is not an exact parcel-level major-accident probability.
